penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A Salesforce AppExchange package or SOQL-based audit tool requires non-trivial Salesforce-platform-specific development (Apex, metadata API, AppExchange security review) that cannot be delivered purely via Claude + prompts + Stripe. Each enterprise deployment also likely requires org-specific config and setup support.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Enterprise Salesforce admins will raise config questions, org permission issues, and edge-case sync-log quirks that require human-judgement responses.

rationale: The buyer is real and well-defined — Salesforce admins at mid-to-large enterprises running active EAC migrations — and they demonstrably pay for Salesforce tooling. However, building a functional bulk-sync audit tool requires Salesforce-platform expertise (Apex/SOQL, metadata API, AppExchange review process) that is well beyond what Claude + a landing page can ship in a week; this is a developer-hours product, not a prompt-plus-Stripe product. Combined with the one-time-utility nature of a migration tool (low recurring revenue) and per-org setup friction, the autonomy and buildability scores pull the total below the validate threshold after penalties.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator using this factory. Building a legitimate Salesforce sync-audit tool would require an Apex developer, AppExchange security review, and org-by-org installation support — none of which the factory can automate. The migration pain is real, but the delivery mechanism is outside the factory's toolset. Drop and do not pursue.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (5, below 6 floor) and operational_autonomy (4, below 7 floor). Even without penalties the build gates would block promotion. Migration utility also has inherently limited recurring revenue.
